case_title: MOHAMMAD MIAN v. STATE OF U.P.
accused_occupation: Owner of a fair price shop
aggravating_circumstances: Long-standing enmity, firing from roof, multiple gunshots
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted of murder charge, convicted under Section 307 IPC
high_court_outcome: Convicted under Section 302 IPC read with Section 34 IPC
neutral_facts: The accused, who owned a fair price shop, had a dispute with the victim over the supply of sugar. The accused fired a shot at the victim, who was then shot dead by the accused's sons from the roof of their house. The victim's son witnessed the incident and lodged an FIR. The prosecution presented eyewitness accounts, medical evidence of gun shot wounds, and a site plan. The trial court acquitted the accused of murder due to discrepancies in the medical evidence, but convicted one accused under Section 307 IPC. The High Court overturned the acquittal, finding the medical evidence supported the eyewitness testimony, and convicted all accused under Section 302 IPC.
